evidence: Defining behaviour graded: multi-user pipeline board and conversations are graded by many functional rows (hro_move_one_stage w1.5, hro_stale_refused w2.5, hro_bulk_all_or_none w2, hro_undo_restores/conflict w2, hro_live_board w2.5, hro_msg_exchange, hro_unread_counts, hro_drafts, hro_candidate_private), matching instruction.md:1-9. Server-backed (not just same-origin): constraints gate hro_gate_shared (gates/constraints/judge.toml:23) and the functional global gate (functional/prompt.md:11) create a job+candidate as Rafael and require the Observer in a NEW independent browser context (browser.newContext, explicitly 'a reload or a second tab of the same context is not independent'; 'a browser-only save fails') to see it - this excludes localStorage/same-origin-only apps. Shared state is re-read cross-account in hro_reorder (Mei independent context), hro_add_candidate, hro_job_open, hro_notes (Aud reads notes). Durability across process restart: hro_restart (functional judge.toml:401-408, protocol D prompt.md:51) records jobs, per-stage order, notes, messages, activity and the seeded Platform Engineer order/note, calls restart_app (template-identical restart_mcp.py relaunches node on the same DB_PATH, test.sh:127-193), signs in again and compares, and detects reseeding/duplication ('starting data is not loaded again'). Reload/re-auth durability where the brief requires it (instruction.md:7, hireops_rules.md:105-106,168-175): hro_drafts (reload, per-conversation), hro_pol_failed_send (unsaved note draft survives reload), hro_pol_session_resume (ended session -> sign-in prompt -> same reply resumes and sends; Mei on same browser sees no drafts; Rafael's drafts back after re-sign-in). Drafts are allowed to be browser-local ('Where drafts are kept is yours'), so the rubric correctly does not demand server storage there. Golden: SQLite at DB_PATH with tables for jobs/applications/messages/reads/notes/activity/actions (db.js:9-53); scripted golden observations (workspace.json groups 14,16,18,20, all passed: draft survives reload, session-ended resume, restart keeps jobs/cards/order/messages/activity without reseeding) - source hashes verified against the frozen bytes. Weak-app probes: (a) localStorage-only app -> fails both gates (independent context sees nothing) -> reward 0; (b) static seed JSON -> gate requires the newly created job to appear -> fails; (c) in-memory server store -> passes gates but hro_restart = 0. Conforming alternatives: server-stored drafts, websocket vs polling, any routes - no criterion forbids them (hro_drafts/hro_pol_session_resume grade outcomes only). Risks kept true: (1) No full configured judge run exists (raw-evidence-index scope: 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent'); restart_app is only called at the very END of a very long protocol (Z..D, judge timeout 9000 s), so on budget exhaustion hro_restart becomes 'NOT EXERCISED' 0 for the golden too - the durability measurement is unmeasured in the configured setting. (2) Weight: an app that keeps everything in memory (violating 'keep new work across restarts', instruction.md:15, integration.md:8-9) loses only hro_restart 1.5/58.5 functional = ~2.6% functional, ~1.5% of total reward; durability is graded but lightly. (3) Gap: hro_restart's comparison list omits per-person read markers/unread counts and seen state (golden persists them in the 'reads' table); an app keeping read markers in memory would reset unread counts on restart without any criterion noticing. Bounded, not a blocker for this row.
counterexample: Not a Fail. Residual weak app: a server that keeps read markers (unread/seen) in process memory while persisting everything else in SQLite; after restart_app every person's unread counts reset, yet hro_restart (which compares jobs, order, notes, messages, activity only) still passes. Also an all-in-memory server loses only ~1.5% of total reward.
suggested_fix: Optional: add 'and Rafael's per-conversation unread count/total' to the D record-and-compare list in hro_restart; consider whether 1.5 weight is adequate for restart durability; obtain a full configured judge run confirming protocol D (restart_app) is reached within the 9000 s budget.
